Hi Thiago, thanks for joining. I want to go over the pumping station before Friday.
Sure. Sorry, the connection is bad. I didn't catch the last part. Could you tell me what you want to go over?
The capacity. The client changed the requirement last week.
I see. Do you know what the new flow rate is?

Okay. Could you tell me why the client changed it?

Let me double-check the numbers and follow up tomorrow.
So, just to clarify, the deadline is still Friday?

I coach engineers who work with teams in other countries, and here is the first thing I tell them. Most problems on international calls are not about English. They are about silence. Somebody does not catch a number, and instead of asking, they say nothing and hope it comes back later. It never does. So ask, and ask early. You do not need a perfect sentence. Sorry, I didn't catch that is enough. If you want to sound more professional, put a polite start in front of your question: could you tell me what the deadline is, do you know if the client approved it. And at the end of every call, take one minute to repeat the action items. It feels slow, but it saves a week of emails.

Hi Thiago, this is Mark from the Houston office. I am calling to follow up on the pumping station. Rachel told me the client wants a higher capacity, and I would like to know if that changes the budget. Could you also tell me when you can send the new specification? The client meeting is on Tuesday, so Monday morning would be ideal. One more thing. I am not sure what the new flow rate is, so please double-check it with your team before you send anything. Call me back when you can, or send me an email. Thanks, and have a good weekend.
